LIMITR uses Android AccessibilityService to detect the package name of the app window you open and display a blocking screen while your timers or intervals are active.

All processing stays on this device. LIMITR does not read screen text, collect screen contents, or send app-window events to a server.

This access is optional. You can disable it in Android Accessibility settings at any time. Timers remain saved while access is off, but blocking is unavailable. Android may interrupt enforcement; LIMITR cannot suspend other apps.
I agree to LIMITR using accessibility access for app blocking.
Enable LIMITR in Android Accessibility settings to block selected apps. You can turn it off at any time.
Usage access shows time spent in apps over the last 24 hours. Statistics stay on this device. Blocking works without this permission.
